title_page_text: Innovation GM / Innovate UK ‘Good to Great’ proposal
Objectives
The project seeks to address analysis of funding application outcomes and feedback from Innovate UK which show that GM-based businesses need to
Apply more
Be more successful
Ask for enough cash

A partnership of Innovate UK. GMCA and Manchester Metropolitan, Manchester and Salford Universities is looking to address this through targeted intervention on businesses across a range of sectors, working with a cohort of both successful and unsuccessful applicants.
Approach and methodology

The Fifth Sector’s proposed approach builds on the success of a previous programme for the Digital & Creative Industries hosted in GM: Accidental Leaders. This was a targeted intervention to ensure that the digital and creative supply chain in the North West was both aware of the strategic opportunities and equipped with the management skills to address the opportunities presented by the planned investment in MediaCity and the BBC move North. It was designed and delivered by Lynne McCadden in her role as Managing Director of Vision+Media, the regional screen agency at the time, and sponsored by Iain Bennett in his role as Sector Leader for Digital & Creative Industries (DCI) at Northwest Regional Development Agency.

Accidental Leaders brought together cohorts of business leaders from all parts of the DCI sector in an approach which combined workshops led by industry specialists and management experts, peer learning groups and mentoring to help founders and senior managers to articulate their product offer and build a strategic approach to investor and business development to bring it to market. Its impact can be observed in the growth of the DCI supply chain in scale and revenue and in increased investment in the sector in GM.
Business Sectors
Businesses should be representative of ALL sectors defined but with a clear focus on:
Advanced Materials and Manufacturing
Net Zero
Digital & Creative

title_page_text: The Fifth Sector has carried out some initial analysis of Innovate UK thematic calls to understand the performance of Greater Manchester companies in securing IUK funding for innovation and R&D across key sectors like manufacturing, digital, creative and net zero. The findings highlight opportunities to increase application rates, success rates and funding amounts through targeted interventions. Ongoing analysis will further examine the characteristics of successful applicants and projects to inform support strategies; but there are significant gaps in the publicly-available data. The level of detail and usefulness of the findings would be greatly enhanced by other kinds of evidence held by Business Connect, GM partners and IUK.
This includes:

Information from Business Connect, GM partners and Universities about their existing interventions with GM businesses. We know that the level of intervention differs by funding stream – for example, universities draft KTP applications on behalf of the business – and it would be useful to be able to compare effectiveness of different approaches.

Names and contacts within intermediary organisations (trade bodies, business support providers, private sector investors) already engaged by GM partners, IUK and Business Connect so we can quickly determine an engagement plan which avoids duplication of effort and builds on existing relationships. This will help accelerate the pilot stage of this work.
Case study examples from universities, GM partners and Business Connect on three tiers of businesses:
Those who do well with applications
Those who have been encouraged to apply but have not to date succeeded
Those who have good ideas which could benefit from R&D investment but have not to date taken the next step to apply to IUK

Subject to agreeing a robust data processing agreement, it would be helpful to have details of all applications, including unsuccessful ones – this will help us to identify the ‘middle tier’ of businesses who have been motivated to make an application but have not yet succeeded to see whether their process can be improved and if so, how. We don’t need any personal data in order to do this – once we have a list of business names, we can use Beauhurst as the basis of further analysis and tracking and would anonymise findings.
Iain Bennett
The Fifth Sector
12 April 2024

title_page_text: Based on the conversation, here is a summary of the key points regarding R&D investment in Manchester:
Current Approach Shortcomings:
1. Lack of connectivity and understanding of the local VC ecosystem among Manchester founders compared to London counterparts.
2. Suboptimal changes to the R&D tax credit system hurt early-stage companies.
3. Insufficient support and poor advice given to early-stage founders after receiving initial funding.
4. Fragmentation and lack of coordination among organizations supporting the ecosystem.
5. Low general awareness and understanding of grants and how to leverage them effectively.
Evidenced Failings and Reasons:
1. Manchester companies often submit lower-quality grant/investment applications compared to London due to a less developed ecosystem and lack of resources/knowledge.
2. Companies get stuck in cycles of being "over-mentored and underfunded", going through the same programs without making substantial progress.
3. Sector-specific challenges, such as Advanced Materials struggling to maintain momentum and visibility compared to more hyped areas like AI.
Recommended Improvements and Alternatives:
1. Increase high-quality, coordinated events and committed organizations working towards common goals.
2. Leverage the brand and resources of the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) to support initiatives and add credibility.
3. Provide targeted education and support to improve the quality of grant/investment applications.

title_page_text: InnovateUK Funding: From Good to Great – Pilot Workshop
Background/Context

In December 2022 Innovation Greater Manchester (IGM), GMCA and Innovate UK signed an MoU in which they agreed to strengthen research clusters and drive innovation in the region, strengthening collaboration and accelerating investment around Long Term innovation developments.
One of the key aims of this MoU is to increase private sector investment in R&D, supported by increasing public sector funding for R&D&I activity, with a particular focus on SMEs.

A key work strand of the MoU is: “Supporting GM businesses to better access innovation funding - principally Innovate (IUK) including by supporting GM businesses to produce more high-quality applications and propositions.

In relation to SMEs, within GM applications to Innovate UK (IUK) competitions have a lower volume and funding levels than the UK national average awards, with average success rates. This results in GM SMEs bringing in less funding than would be expected.
This Pilot workshop

Innovate UK already provide call specific publicity and support for specific calls and enduring funding programmes (SMART etc) to broad groups of applicants, whilst Innovate Edge, The Growth Company and others provide 1:1 tailored funding support for regional businesses and SMEs (IUK funding & beyond).
From a GM perspective there is a real need to understand:
(1) What are the experiences of GM business in either successfully securing Innovate UK funding, or getting close – high scoring, unsuccessful applications?
(2) What is the appetite from business to continue to pursue this funding stream?
(3) Is there a “GM advantage” – critical mass, connectivity etc – and is it being communicated/leveraged?
(4) What support do GM businesses require (& is it already there/accessible)?
(5) How could/should these learning be integrated in GM strategy and planning.
The workshop will include representation from GMCA, IUK, Growth Company/Innovate Edge and regional Universities: Manchester Met, University of Manchester & University of Salford

Overall Feedback on the Workshop @ 0:00

Michael thought the workshop was very good overall, with strong presentations from the speakers. He particularly enjoyed the enthusiasm and creative approach of the presenter from Vector Group. However, he noted that the slides were too small for the audience to see clearly.

Michael felt that while the university and business support organizations were intended to be partners, there was sometimes a sense that the university saw itself as superior. Michael suggested having more practical, hands-on content, such as presentations from successful grant applicants walking through the full process. He also recommended breaking into smaller discussion groups facilitated by the organizers to allow for more personalized support and Q&A.

Michael found the workshop materials shared afterwards to be helpful, and would like to see more of his colleagues be able to attend future sessions. He is interested in pursuing additional funding opportunities through Innovate UK and the DCMS.

Lynne thanked Michael for his time and feedback, noting that the partners would likely take some time to organize another workshop based on the learnings from this pilot. She wished Michael the best of luck with any future funding applications.

title_page_text: Strategic Analysis: Greater Manchester R&D Funding Process Optimisation

This analysis builds on feedback from the initial “From Good To Great” workshop held at Man Met in May 2025. It complements direct feedback with a comprehensive business process analysis that positions GM Combined Authority to argue for devolved funding variations as a better way to improve outcomes.
Current State vs. Desired State
Underlying Process Gaps
The workshop feedback revealed three critical systemic issues that mask deeper structural problems:
1. Pre-Qualification Gap
Current: SMEs enter funding competitions without adequate business case validation
Impact: High failure rates, wasted resources, poor ROI on ecosystem support
Evidence: "The how-to was useful... but would have been more useful before we had a bid"
2. Strategic Alignment Gap
Current: Irregular, seemingly subjective call timing disconnected from regional priorities
Impact: Missed opportunities, reactive rather than proactive innovation pipeline
Evidence: Participants struggling with timing and relevance of available funding
3. Supply Chain Investment Gap
Current: Large companies limited to 50% cost recovery, creating collaboration barriers

title_page_text: From Good to Great: Innovation Funding Support Session
Summary

The innovation funding workshop demonstrated significant potential as a collaborative platform, bringing together key stakeholders from the Manchester ecosystem including GMCA, Growth Hub, universities, and businesses. While participants valued the practical guidance and networking opportunities, several structural challenges emerged that require attention to maximize future impact.
Key Strengths and Successes
Practical content delivery

The workshop's greatest strength lay in its practical approach to bid writing guidance. Participants consistently highlighted the value of tangible, actionable advice over theoretical presentations. One attendee noted that they particularly appreciated "succinct advice" and understanding, "there's a reason that went down well" when discussing successful bid examples. This practical focus resonated strongly with businesses seeking immediate, applicable insights.
Ecosystem collaboration

The event successfully created a collaborative environment. The convergence of universities, businesses, and support organisations in a single forum provided valuable opportunities for cross-sector understanding and partnership development.
As one participant observed,
"The strongest element was the whole Manchester ecosystem working together."
Networking impact
